title: Using Nanoplasmon-Enhanced Scattering and Low-Magnification Microscope Imaging to Quantify Tumor-Derived Exosomes
protocol: Wash 40 μL of AuNR-AV (2.56 x 10¹¹ particles) three times with 200 μL PBS (pH 7.0) by centrifugation and aspiration (8,500 x g at 4 °C for 10 minutes).
Suspend the AuNR-AV pellet in 40 μL PBS after final wash.
Mix this AuNR-AV suspension with 10 μL biotinylated antibody (0.5 mg/mL) and 150 μL of PBS at 4 °C for 2 h using a mixer to allow neutravidin-biotin binding to reach completion.
Wash the resulting antibody-conjugated AuNRs three times by centrifugation and aspiration (6,500 x g at 4 °C for 10 minutes).
Suspend them in 200 μL PBS after washing.
Store them at 4 °C until use.
Dilute selected exosome capture antibodies to 0.025 mg/mL in PBS.
Add 1 µL/well of the diluted antibody onto a multi-well protein A/G slide.
Incubate the slide at 37 °C for 1 h in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate wells to remove unbound antibodies.
Wash wells three times by adding and aspirating 1 µL/well of PBS.
Load each well with 1 µL of blocking buffer and incubate the slide for 2 h at 37 °C in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate wells to remove blocking buffer.
Wash wells three times by adding and aspirating 1 µL/well of PBS.
Immediately use the blocked slides for exosome capture and analysis.
Culture cells for 48 hours at 37 °C in serum-free culture media to allow exosome accumulation in the media.
Isolate cell culture supernatants by centrifugation of suspension cultures or direct aspiration of culture media from adherent cell cultures.
Centrifuge the collected media at 2000 x g for 30 min to remove debris and recover the supernatant.
Filter the clarified culture supernatant through a 0.45 µm low protein binding filter unit.
Concentrate the resulting filtrate by centrifugation at 3200 x g using a 100,000 nominal molecular weight limit filter system to a 250 µL final volume.
Collect the retained volume from this filter and wash the filter with 200 µL PBS, then combine this wash volume with the collected exosome sample volume.
Centrifuge this sample at 21,000 x g for 45 minutes and carefully recover the supernatant without collecting any precipitated material.
Centrifuge the recovered supernatant at 100,000 x g for 3 hours to precipitate the exosomes.
Aspirate away the supernatant and collect the exosome pellet in 100 µL PBS.
Store the resulting exosome suspensions at 4 °C if used within 24 hours or at -80 °C for long term storage.

Quantify an aliquot of the exosome suspension after mixing by direct measurement of exosome numbers using nanoparticle tracking analysis, tunable resistive pulse sensing, or micro-bicinchoninic acid assay.
Generate a set of serial dilutions of the exosome suspension to allow comparison of nanoparticle signal to input exosome number or protein content.
Transfer 1 μL of each exosome standard to each of its replicate wells on the assay plate.
Collect plasma or serum samples by standard methods and store at -80 °C until needed for exosome analysis.
Rapidly thaw samples in a room temperature water bath.
Repetitively mix the thawed samples by inversion to promote homogenous suspension.
Centrifuge plasma or serum samples at 500 x g for 15 min.
Transfer an aliquot of the centrifuged sample to a fresh tube.
Add PBS to generate a 1:1 dilution of the plasma or serum sample.
Mix the diluted sample by gentle vortexing or inversion.
Transfer 1 µL of each diluted plasma or serum sample to assay plate wells.
Load wells of a blocked EV capture slide with 1 µL/well of exosome sample.
Incubate the slide overnight at 4 °C in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate all sample wells after incubation.
Add 1 µL/well of PBS to wash wells and remove unbound exosomes.
Load sample wells with 1 µL/well of AuNR-IgG suspension.
Incubate the slide for 2 h at 37 °C in a humidified chamber.
Aspirate the nanoparticle solution after incubation.
Wash the slide in PBS supplemented with 0.01% Tween-20 (PBST) for 10 min.
Wash all sample wells with deionized water for 10 min.
Air-dry the slide for subsequent LMDFM imagery.
Capture images for exosome quantification under consistent lighting using a digital camera attached to a microscope equipped with a dark-field condenser.
Open the image capture software.
Place the slide upside down on the microscope stage.
Adjust the slide position.
Apply a small drop of immersion oil on the back of the slide, where the condenser lens contacts the slide.
Click the live button in the software interface.
Adjust the exposure time against a high concentration standard well to ensure the image is not saturated.
Open the Scan Large Image window from the Acquire tab.
Set the Macro Image Optical conf to current.
Set the Objective: 2:10x for Macro Image.
Set the Scanning Optical conf to current.
Set the Objective: 2:10x for Scanning.
Set the Stitching Overlap to 20%.
Set the Stitching via to Optimal Path.
Choose Create Large Image setting in the microscope software.
Close active shutter during stage movement.
Wait before each Capture: 20 ms.
Focus manually at start.
Use step-by-step focus every 20 field.
Move the microscope stage to define the left top right bottom limits of the target scan field.
Adjust the focus to achieve a clear image on the monitor.
Adjust condenser settings and environmental lighting as necessary to minimize any lighting irregularities in the focused image.
Name the image output file in the software.
Click the Scan button to allow the microscope to scan and create and save a stitched image of the entire slide.
Open the saved image with the image capture software you are using.
Save the image at 1/8 scale for subsequent analysis on the DSM plugin in ImageJ.
Open the saved image from section 6.8 with ImageJ.
Choose the DSM Scan button from the Plugins tab.
Define the number of columns and rows according to the opened image.
Set Resize Percentage = 25.
Set Spot Diameter (in pixels) = 190 – 200.
Set Diameter Range = 32.
Set Increment diameter (in pixels) = 8.
Set DSM Configuration - Low limit = 0.
Set DSM Configuration - High limit = 62.
Set Adjacent Distance = 100.
Set Subtract Bias = 0.
